item.title: Meta’s Muse Spark Open now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
item.abstract: Muse Spark Open, Meta’s coding-optimized open-weight model, is now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart , the machine learning (ML) hub of Amazon SageMaker AI . The model was trained on real developer workflows, such as multi-file refactors and long debugging sessions, and it supports a context window of 1 million tokens. You can deploy it to a SageMaker AI endpoint in your own AWS account in a few steps, without managing the serving infrastructure yourself. SageMaker JumpStart offers two variants: BF16 ( Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B ) and NVFP4 quantized ( Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4 ). In this post, we introduce Muse Spark Open and show you how to deploy the model with Amazon SageMaker Studio and the SageMaker Python SDK , send it a first inference request, and clean up. Meta describes Muse Spark Open as a coding-optimized model trained for agentic coding workflows, with a focus on first-attempt accuracy, tool calling, and understanding of large codebases. It’s a reasoning model, and it accepts text, images, documents, audio, and audio-video as input and returns text. Muse Spark Open uses a mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture with 816 billion total parameters, of which 42 billion are active for each token. The model holds the capacity of a very large network, while the compute it spends on each token is closer to that of a much smaller dense model. Meta releases the weights under the Muse Model License, which includes the Muse Spark Usage Policy. The following table summarizes the model. Meta trained Muse Spark Open on the way developers work in real repositories: code generation, debugging, multi-file refactors, and tasks that run for a long time. With the 1 million-token context window, the model can take in a whole project, including its dependencies, legacy code, and thousands of files. You don’t need to split a task into smaller pieces to fit the context. Meta also designed Muse Spark Open as an agentic model from the start. Meta says the model plans, acts, observes the result, and corrects itself over long horizons, rather than making single tool calls. As a reasoning model, it works through a task before it acts, and the SageMaker AI endpoint returns that reasoning alongside the answer, so you can follow what an agent is doing and why. Meta trained the model to browse the web, coordinate subagents for work that can be split up, and operate computers across desktop, mobile, and browser environments. These are capabilities of the model. On SageMaker AI, your application or agent framework provides the tools, browser, and computer-use environment that the model calls. Beyond code, Meta reports that Muse Spark Open reasons across images, documents, audio, and video. Two properties of the model shape how you serve it. First, sparse activation keeps per-token compute low, but serving still requires enough GPU memory to hold all 816 billion parameters, so the instance choice comes down to memory capacity. Second, the NVFP4 variant stores weights in NVIDIA’s 4-bit floating point format, which needs roughly a quarter of the memory of the BF16 weights. On SageMaker AI, that difference decides the instance: the NVFP4 variant runs on ml.p5e.48xlarge , and the BF16 variant runs on ml.p6-b300.48xlarge . That makes NVFP4 the variant to try first when you size for cost. Evaluate it on your own workloads to confirm the quality fits your use case. With open weights on SageMaker AI, you also control the deployment. The endpoint runs in your AWS account, so your source code and prompts are processed on infrastructure that you configure and control. You can attach the endpoint to your own Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) , encrypt its storage volume with a key from AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) , and turn on network isolation for the container. You also choose the instance type and scaling limits, and you pin the model version, so the model only changes when you redeploy. You can use Muse Spark Open for a wide range of applications. Meta’s focus on coding and agentic workflows suits it to the following use cases: You can deploy Muse Spark Open from SageMaker Studio or with the SageMaker Python SDK. item.title: CopilotKit Releases CLiF: A Continual Learning Platform That Turns Agent Traces and User Actions into Skills, Evals, and Fine-Tuning Data
item.abstract: Teams shipping AI agents at scale keep running into the same pattern. Even agents built on top-tier models like Fable and Astra struggle to carry out complex, end-to-end tasks inside a specific product consistently enough to deploy. So teams grind out evals for the workflows that matter most, often hundreds or thousands of hand-written cases, and then improve the agent bit by bit through prompt edits, harness fixes, and special cases until it passes enough of them to go live. Meanwhile, the product’s own users carry out those same tasks every day, and know which actions to take and in what order. CopilotKit, the company behind the open-source CopilotKit framework and the AG-UI protocol, released CLiF , a platform for continual learning from full-stack trajectories, in early access . CLiF securely captures what the agent does and what users do in the product, and turns that record into skills, production-based evals, and fine-tuning datasets, all exportable along with the raw trajectories. CopilotKit is open source , with more than 38,000 stars on GitHub. Most agent observability today is centered on the agent. Tracing tools capture prompts, tool calls, and model outputs, which shows where the agent went wrong while leaving the correct path out of view. Product analytics covers the other side with clicks, funnels, and session replays, though that data is built for a person reading a dashboard rather than for teaching an agent a task or testing it. In most production agent stacks, the two never end up on the same timeline. That gap matters because the agent learns a product from prompts, skills, tool descriptions, and exposed APIs, and has to work out on its own how those pieces fit together for a real task. The people using the product have already solved that, often hundreds of times. CopilotKit’s view, laid out in its explainer on agent learning , is that how users actually get work done is the most valuable dataset any agent team has, and that it is rarely captured in a form an agent can learn from. CLiF is part of CopilotKit Intelligence and is built around a single primitive, the full-stack trajectory. It is captured through AG-UI (Agent-User Interaction Protocol) , the open protocol CopilotKit created to connect agents to user-facing applications. Because AG-UI sits between the agent and the user on any surface, it can see both sides of a task: Together, that is a full-stack trajectory. AG-UI already streams the agent’s events to the frontend, so securely capturing user actions over the same protocol puts both halves in one stream from the start, with no separate analytics pipeline to stitch them together later. Each user session becomes a single trajectory that a team can open in CopilotKit Intelligence and replay step by step, with clicks, server requests, and agent messages in the order they happened. CopilotKit describes the learning loop in four stages. 1. Capture. Trajectories stream into CopilotKit Intelligence and are assigned to learning containers, which scope learning to one kind of work, such as billing support or customer onboarding. The runtime picks the container for each session through the getTrajectoryLearningContainerIds callback, and sessions can be moved in or out of a container later in the Intelligence UI. Each container learns only from its own sessions. 2. Find patterns. Analysis runs on a schedule once a container passes a set threshold of new sessions, and teams can also trigger it manually. Each run works from a frozen snapshot of the container’s sessions and surfaces Insights: recurring requests, repeated corrections, and the friction users quietly work around. CopilotKit sees that friction as the strongest signal, since it tends to repeat across thousands of sessions and shows exactly what the agent should learn next. Every Insight cites the specific events behind it and links straight to the source trajectory. 3. Review. When the evidence supports a reusable lesson, CLiF proposes it as a skill, written as a plain SKILL.md file. The analysis service cannot publish anything on its own: a person approves or rejects each proposal, either in the Intelligence UI or through the CopilotKit CLI. Published skills are versioned and can be retired at any time. 4. Deliver and export. Published skills reach the agent without a redeploy, and teams that need stability can pin the agent to a fixed skill revision. For any other agent or MCP server, skills can be downloaded as plain files with copilotkit skills download <container> –output <dir>. The trajectories themselves can be exported as raw event data from the Intelligence dashboard. For early access teams, the same pipeline also produces eval candidates and fine-tuning datasets from these trajectories. On the agent side, CLiF builds on Automatic Learning , the capability in CopilotKit Intelligence that CopilotKit also positions as the foundation for self-improving agents . Automatic Learning learns from the conversations users have with the agent. CLiF extends the same loop to product trajectories, so it also learns from the work users do directly in the product, outside the chat. Every agent conversation is stored in full through AG-UI Streams : messages, tool calls, generative UI, state, approvals, and files. Developers choose which threads count as evidence by returning a container ID from the getLearningContainerId callback on the CopilotKit runtime, which is the agent-side counterpart to the trajectory callback. Teams that already have an agent in production can import existing history from a LangGraph Server or LangSmith Deployment instead of starting from zero. Skill delivery works through adapters for LangGraph (Python and TypeScript), Mastra, Google ADK, Microsoft Agent Framework, CopilotKit’s built-in agent, and more. The adapter adds a catalog and two tools, copilotkit_load_skill and copilotkit_read_skill_file, and the model loads a skill when the task calls for it. Developer instructions keep precedence, so skills cannot override the agent’s role, safety rules, or tool restrictions. Skills are only the first output. The same trajectories feed four outputs in total, all exportable into a team’s existing stack: CopilotKit’s view is that teams should keep the eval and observability tools they already use, and CLiF supplies the data those tools have been missing. Say you’re the CTO of a project management platform similar to Linear, where engineering teams plan sprints and track issues. You want agents to take over routine work in your product and do it reliably, both your own built-in agent and external agents like Claude that customers connect through your MCP server. Sprint close-out is one of the first tasks on the list. Your platform already has a one-click option that moves every unfinished issue into the next sprint, and your docs describe close-out exactly that way. So an agent asked to close out a sprint does just that, and moves every unfinished issue forward. Once CLiF is securely capturing product trajectories, thousands of close-outs show that team leads on your platform do more than that. Most use the one-click option, then spend the next few minutes fixing the result: Nobody on your team designed this routine, and few users would describe it if asked. It exists only in the clicks and requests that follow the one-click move. Agent traces never see it, because users do it themselves. Product analytics records the extra clicks without their meaning, and spotting the pattern in session replays would mean watching thousands of recordings. CLiF surfaces the routine as an Insight, citing the exact sessions behind it, and proposes a skill for the full close-out. After your team reviews and publishes it, your built-in agent picks it up without a redeploy, and you ship the same skill with your MCP server so Claude and other connected agents follow it too.

item.abstract:

Original SVGs from Simon Willison’s runs · highest reasoning setting that returned an SVG When they could look like these? This is the LLM diversity collapse problem no one is talking about. Despite rapid advances in their ability to generate functional websites and product UIs, leading AI models still struggle to make creative design decisions. We evaluated 16 frontier models across 80 open-ended UI tasks, each adapted to two distinct product domains alongside human designer references. Existing UI benchmarks often measure a single output quality metric. Instead, we measure three dimensions of design creativity: – Originality: How distinct a model's designs are from other models' outputs for the same brief. – Creative Range: How much a model adapts its design decisions when the product domain changes. – Appropriateness: How well the generated UI satisfies the functional requirements of the brief. The results reveal a substantial gap in overall creativity: The best model, @OpenAI GPT-6 Astra, scores 65.5 against a human reference of 92.3. item.title: 量子位智庫釋出Agent落地報告！拆解企業智慧化六大斷點，附全鏈路破局框架
item.abstract: 量子位智庫釋出Agent落地報告！拆解企業智慧化六大斷點，附全鏈路破局框架 思邈 2026-10-15 16:48:31 來源： 量子位 Agent究竟該如何深入業務毛細血管？ 量子位智庫 公眾號AI123All 過去這一年，幾乎沒有哪家企業不在高喊“全面擁抱AI”。 Chatbot上了，Agent也用了，內部彙報裡“效率提升XX%”的數字越來越好看。 但如果去問業務負責人一個樸素的問題——缺貨少了嗎？交付快了嗎？客戶滿意度漲了嗎？答案往往沒那麼確定。 事實上，絕大多數企業的智慧化轉型，正集體遭遇一場“虛假繁榮”。我們習慣了把AI當成個人提效工具，卻忽略了一個殘酷的真相： 個人任務的高效，並不等同於企業經營價值的兌現。 如果AI無法真正打通 資料、判斷、行動與系統控制 的全鏈路閉環，企業的智慧化就只能永遠卡在規模化應用的最後一公里。 企業級AI的下半場，究竟該如何破局？Agent又該如何真正深入業務毛細血管，完成面向未來的系統性重構？ 近日，量子位智庫正式釋出報告 《Agent驅動的企業智慧化：單點提效到規模化重塑》 。在這份報告中，我們試圖撥開大模型落地的迷霧，尋找企業智慧化規劃的全新解法。 AI用起來了，但卡在哪？ 企業AI落地過程中容易卡住的地方，用一個場景就能串起來看： 門店缺貨風險處置 。 同一個經營分析助手，技術團隊覺得報告生成了就算完成，業務人員覺得原因查清了才算交代，管理者關心的是缺貨到底有沒有減少——三方的完成標準壓根對不上。 資料層面也有類似的錯位，賬面上顯示有庫存，但已分配的、凍結的扣掉之後，真正能調的量和系統裡那個數字差得不少。AI拿著賬面數字去做判斷，起點就是歪的。 即使資料準了、分析對了，建議到執行之間還隔著人工填單、提交審批、跟蹤配送這一整條鏈路。建議進了系統並不等於事情辦完了，而完成狀態能不能回傳給AI，決定了任務閉環能不能真正合上。 更不用說每一步操作背後都涉及 誰有權發起、誰來審批、出了問題誰來接管 這些權責問題。 這類斷點一共被歸納出六個： 任務定義、資料可信度、判斷的可驗證性、行動落地、許可權責任劃分，以及價值衡量與複製 。 每個單獨看都不致命，但串在一起，就解釋了為什麼很多企業的AI專案停在了“局部能用、整體推不動”的狀態。 這些沒完成的工作，最終還是回到了人的手裡，變成漫長的返工、等待和兜底。 那麼，企業究竟該如何系統性地破除這些盲區？ 一套圍繞業務結果的全鏈路框架 既然局部的小修小補無法解決根本問題，企業該如何重構一套行之有效的智慧化解法？ 量子位智庫在報告中提出，成熟的企業級Agent絕不僅是一個孤立的問答工具，而必須具備 貫通任務、上下文、判斷、行動、控制與衡量的“全鏈路能力” 。 其中，一切智慧決策的起點，在於打破資料孤島，建立起 真正可信的上下文環境 。 很多時候，AI之所以在業務分析中顯得“不夠聰明”，根本原因在於底層資料和業務語義的脫節——欄位定義混亂、版本口徑不一，AI自然無法給出靠譜的結論。 要想讓Agent真正成為懂業務的“參謀”，必須先讓資料從單純的“能查到”進化為全鏈路的“可信賴”。 在這方面，一些領先的技術實踐為行業提供了很好的範本。例如網易智企旗下的資料智慧品牌 數帆 ，通過其開發治理一體化平臺 EasyData ，將資料開發、質量、安全與業務治理深度融合，為Agent穩定輸送了高質量、可追溯的資產語義。 在此基礎上，依託網易智企· 知數DataAgent ，企業能夠將分散的指標、知識庫與自然語言查詢無縫打通，讓AI真正聽懂業務語言。 在實際落地中，這種全鏈路的貫通正在釋放業務勢能。以 三花智控 為例，藉助數帆在底層統一資料與語義口徑，AI能夠自動拉取預實資料並識別偏差，將原本耗時 2-3小時 的預算分析大幅壓縮至 10分鐘 ，讓財務團隊從繁重的報表處理轉向深度的業務研判。 而當智慧化從分析決策走向更深處的 軟體工程與應用交付 時，新的挑戰隨之出現：如何避免Coding Agent開發應用時的需求走樣與前後端聯調費時？ 一個值得關注的變化是，企業正在嘗試把AI開發從“自由生成”拉回到更可控的工程流程中。 以 網易智企·CodeWave SDD（規格驅動開發，Spec-Driven Development）為例，其核心思路並不是讓AI直接“開寫”，而是把交付拆成需求、架構、開發、測試、釋出、交付多級逐級傳導： 業務需求先轉化為結構化規格，再向下推導技術設計與任務拆分，最後才進入程式碼生成。 每一環都有明確的輸入輸出和校驗卡點，使需求澄清、開發、測試到釋出的全流程始終可控、可追溯。 這種“逐級傳導”恰好對應了市面上常見SDD方案的三處斷點：規格寫法不標準、缺少澄清機制，對大模型只是軟約束；需求一複雜就撐爆上下文視窗，引發遺忘與幻覺；能力又只覆蓋研發一段，需求與交付兩頭落空。 CodeWave SDD則逐一補齊，以EARS標準化需求格式並顯式澄清歧義，用模組化拆分與細粒度子任務隔離上下文、化整為零，再把需求、設計、編碼、測試到釋出串成多角色協同的端到端鏈路。 這種方式已經開始在實際專案中體現出效率價值。比如， 空格數智科技 在其新能源CRM專案中，將開發週期從60人天縮短至16人天； 上海企通數字科技 在其BIMS系統開發中實現約2.5倍提效，功能首次可用率達到78.63%。 跑通一個Demo容易，複製100次才是真本事 框架有了，下一個問題是怎麼起步。 很多企業的做法是鋪開試點、多線並進，量子位智庫給出的建議是： 先選一個高價值場景，把閉環跑通，再考慮擴展。 選場景有五個篩選維度： 聽起來是常識，但實際操作中很多團隊是反過來的——哪個技術上容易做就先做哪個，做完發現業務價值不大，推廣也就沒了動力。 選定場景之後，試點階段要做的事情比想像中細緻。 現有流程裡哪些環節可以交給系統處理，哪些仍需人工複核，異常情況怎麼走，這些都需要重新設計而不是簡單疊加。 一個容易踩的坑是，保留全部舊流程再額外加上AI結果的檢查，結果整體投入反而增加了。 試點跑完之後，企業往往會面臨三個選擇： 但真正決定企業能不能從“1”走向“100”的，還在後面—— 把第一次成功留下來的經驗，沉澱成可以反覆複用的智慧資產。 比如已經驗證過的指標口徑、介面元件、審批規則、異常樣本，不必每換一個場景就重新做一遍。新的任務可以直接複用這些公共能力，只針對具體業務做必要調整。 所以，規模化複製的本質，是讓第2次、第10次、第100次建設時，都能站在前一次的基礎上繼續往前走。 免費獲取完整報告 企業智慧化走到今天，拉開差距的，其實是企業能不能把模型能力接進業務、組織和流程，最終變成看得見的經營結果。 好的智慧化規劃，從來不是從工具出發，而是需要“ 從業務結果向前追溯 ”；而面向未來的Agent，核心更在於做到“ 人定邊界，AI推進 ”。 這份報告提供的，恰好是這樣一個 從診斷問題、搭建框架到落地驗證的完整思路 。 無論你是正在推進AI試點的業務負責人，還是被要求“用AI提效”但不知道怎麼衡量結果的技術團隊，又或者是需要在規模化階段協調多方職責的管理者，大機率都能在裡面找到對應當前階段的參考。 很多細節，比如怎麼定義任務的完成標準、怎麼設計前後對照的衡量方式、怎麼把試點成果沉澱為可複用的資產……文章裡沒有做一一展開，但可能正是你當前卡住的那個環節。 完整報告可在下方連結 免費下載 ： https://jkhbjkhb.feishu.cn/wiki/W5D7wuDcbiPXDLkaRLQcAJpOn8f 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 Agent 企業智慧化
